question.question: 귀로 소리가 전해지는 길 하나를 묻습니다. 녹음한 내 목소리는 평소보다 높고 얇게 들려 어색합니다. 말할 때 내 목소리는 공기뿐 아니라 머리뼈의 떨림으로도 속귀에 닿는데, 뼈는 낮은 소리를 더 잘 실어 나르기 때문입니다. 이렇게 소리가 전해지는 방식은?
question.explanation: 1923년 휴고 건스백이 이 원리를 쓴 보청기 '오소폰'을 내놓았다. 바깥 소리를 함께 들을 수 있어 운동용 헤드폰으로도 쓰인다.

Bone conduction is one reason why a person's voice sounds different to them when it is recorded and played back. Because the skull conducts lower frequencies better than air, people perceive their own voices to be lower and fuller than others do, and a recording of one's own voice frequently sounds higher than one expects.

Ludwig van Beethoven was famously rumored to be using bone conduction after losing most of his hearing, by placing one end of a rod in his mouth and resting the other end on the rim of his piano. / ...as with bone-conduction headphones—or as a treatment option for certain types of hearing impairment.

In 1923, Hugo Gernsback created a new kind of bone conduction hearing aid called the "Osophone" / leaving the ears free to pick up sound from the environment, users can listen to audio while maintaining greater situational awareness
